title: Emission contract and rollback criteria for function invocations
creator: Claire Nguyen
description: Goal: Define deterministic acceptance criteria for streamed structured outputs that include function/tool invocations, with explicit rollback and resume semantics for partially emitted fragments. This ticket covers: schema envelope format (with versioned annotations), checkpoint markers for resumability, error classification (recoverable vs fatal), idempotency guarantees for function calls, per-fragment latency SLOs, and observability/telemetry required for safe rollouts. Deliverables: an acceptance checklist, example canonical envelopes (success, partial+checkpoint, fatal-error), guidance for SDKs and console display, and a short test matrix the runtime/SDK teams can use to validate behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Schema: All streamed emissions must be wrapped in a versioned envelope: {"envelope_v":"v1", "fragment_id": <uuid>, "seq": <int>, "type": ["meta"|"payload"|"checkpoint"|"error"], "payload": <object>|null, "sig": <optional base64>. The runtime and SDKs must accept v1 and log unknown fields without failing.

Partial emissions + checkpointing: When a long structured response is produced, the runtime must emit checkpoint fragments at configurable maximum byte or token boundaries. Checkpoints must include the last_successful_seq and a resume_token (stable opaque string). Resume semantics: if a client reconnects with a valid resume_token, the runtime must replay from last_successful_seq or provide a deterministic synthesized delta to reach the same final object state.

Idempotent function calls: Function/tool invocations that are emitted as part of the stream must carry an idempotency_key (client or runtime-supplied). If a resume or retry occurs, the function invocation must not be executed more than once for the same idempotency_key unless explicitly requested. Runtime must surface a retried_call boolean in the envelope when retries happen.

Error classification: Define three error classes in acceptance tests: recoverable (transient infra, allow resume/retry), degraded (partial schema validation failures, allow application-level reconciliation), and fatal (non-recoverable: model meltdown, security violation). Each emitted error envelope must include an error_code, class: [recoverable|degraded|fatal], and suggested_action: [retry|resume-with-manual-merge|abort].

Deterministic merge strategy: For partial-object emissions (fragments that update a single logical object), the platform must define and document the merge strategy used on resume: last-writer-wins by seq, with explicit field-level tombstones for deletions. Acceptance tests must include interleaved fragments and validate final object equivalence across: (a) single uninterrupted stream, (b) stream with resume/replay, and (c) stream with a checkpoint and replay from SDK.

Latency SLOs: The runtime must satisfy 95th percentile latency targets for fragment emission (finalization latency) and for checkpoint creation. Acceptance requires: fragment emit 95p < 250ms after token finalization, checkpoint creation 95p < 800ms for standard sized responses (<= 8k tokens). Tests must be included in the perf runbook.

Backpressure & flow control: SDKs must support a simple acks protocol where the client can acknowledge checkpoint fragments. Runtime must pause aggressive batching when unacked checkpoints exceed a configurable threshold. Acceptance tests include simulated slow clients to confirm runtime does not exceed memory limits and resumes correctly.

Observability: Every envelope must emit telemetry fields that flow to tracing and metrics: fragment_size_bytes, seq, fragment_type, resume_token_present (boolean), function_call_id (if present), error_class. Dashboards must show resumed sessions rate, retry count distribution, and fraction of streams that used checkpoint-based resume.

Migration & versioning: v1 envelope must be backward-tolerant: unknown fields ignored and unknown envelope_v values logged but not rejected. Acceptance requires a migration plan doc for v2 with deprecation windows (90 days) and a compatibility test harness.

Security: If a resume_token is produced, it must be opaque, bound to the session/customer, time-limited (configurable TTL, default 10m), and optionally signed with tenant-specific key. Acceptance requires a short threat model and a note that resume tokens cannot contain plaintext PII.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: tight semantics for deterministic resume increase runtime complexity (KV of per-stream fragments) vs improved customer UX for long-running compositional outputs. We recommend an opt-in checkpointing default for >= 4k tokens.

Design decision: Use opaque resume_token signed by control plane to avoid exposing internal offsets. SDKs will translate resume_token to runtime-replay requests; control plane enforces TTL and tenant-scoping.
Implementation hint for ENG: store minimal per-stream index (fragment_id -> seq, last_ack_time) rather than full object to reduce state. Full rehydration done by replaying fragments when necessary.
Example test vectors attached in links; runtime tests should include glitch injection (dropped fragments, duplicate fragments) to validate idempotency logic.
review_comments: PM review (Claire): Please add a simple UX note for console when a stream is resumed (show resume badge + reason).
Eng review (Priya Shah): Concerned about storage cost at high QPS for maintaining resume tokens; suggest TTL and sampling for long-tail debugging.
Design review (Evan Park): Recommend showing partial object preview in Console with clear legend for 'stable' vs 'tentative' fields when stream is not finalized.
Action: add a small canary plan for Dedicated customers to opt into checkpointed streaming before broad rollout.
